title: My Escape from Slavery
summary: This is Frederick Douglass's account of his daring escape from slavery in Maryland to freedom in the North. The narrative details the risks, deceptions, and help he received while fleeing through several slave states on a train, then crossing into Delaware and finally reaching New York. After briefly experiencing the challenges of being newly free—loneliness, danger, and economic hardship—he recounts his subsequent life as a freeman in New Bedford, Massachusetts, where he begins to build a new identity, earn a living at his trade, and confront racial prejudice despite Northern prosperity. Douglass also includes reflections on Reconstruction after the Civil War, emphasizing the need for equal rights and protections for all citizens, black and white.
